title: Alternate Reality Scenarios
thesis: The visitor changes one driver of a world (a resource, a constraint, an accident of history) and the lab grows the technologies that branch from it, each with what it needs, the pressure that forced it at its moment and its cost, checked by Luis's own worldbuilding method (the Necessity Principle: every step needs what came before it; the Orthogonal Path: no step may sit unchanged in Earth's history) against a sourced ledger of Earth's technology. Each branch ends in an artifact Earth never built, its form computed from its lineage and rendered, standing beside Earth's device for the same job, with one line saying which branch the evidence favours. At level 10 the visitor grows a world era by era, each success planting the next era's trouble, keeps it and shares it, and the lab's chains are shown by a committed test to need their driver where Earth-mimicry and grafted reasons do not.

axes.name: Branch growth from a driver
axes.metric: How a world's lineage comes to exist: the count of steps typed by hand in a world file against steps the lab derives from a typed driver; the number of shipped drivers and of the six domains they cover (energy, materials, communication, transport, food, environment); whether a driver the visitor states, absent from every shipped world, grows a complete lineage; whether the same engine regrows Earth's history when no driver is changed; and the number of eras a world grows. A step is a technology node after the driver; the root, the driver and the artifact are not steps, so step 1 is the first technology after the driver.
axes.how_checked: Read the engine and every world file, and count the steps each world file types. State 5 drivers of your own, one in each of 5 domains, none present in the data, and read each lineage the page grows. Run the lab's tests and read the Earth regrowth test. Rungs are cumulative: a rung holds only when every rung below it holds.
ladder: No lineage exists on the page.

One world's lineage (a driver, at least 5 technologies with their parent links, an artifact at the tip) is read from a hand-written data file and drawn, and every parent link resolves to a node of that file.
At least 3 shipped worlds with different drivers, in at least 2 of the six domains; each lineage runs at least 5 steps between the driver and the artifact, and each step lists what it needs.

The lab grows at least one lineage from a typed driver record (a resource or condition, removed or multiplied, with its domain), either by an engine over a table of technologies (each with its function, its needs and what it provides) under a stated rule such as "a technology enters when every need is met by the world or by an earlier step", or by a model whose reply passes a check in code that every need of every step resolves to the driver, the world's starting state or an earlier step; no step of that lineage is typed in a world file.

Grown lineages carry combination and consequence: at least one step of each has two parents (two threads that meet), each branch is followed at least 3 steps past its first technology, and each lineage names its function (the job) and ends at an artifact node for that function.

Level 5, the fiction made real: a driver the visitor states or composes, absent from every shipped world, grows a lineage at the central scene's detail (at least 5 steps between the driver and the artifact, each with its needs, its why-now pressure and its cost; at least one combination; no step marked as Earth-mimicry by the Orthogonal Path test of method-checks rung 5; a seed of trouble at the tip), and then one more era from that seed of trouble, which becomes the new era's pressure, with at least one step that needs a technology of the era before it. For 5 drivers the rater chooses, in 5 of the six domains, every lineage is complete and no two of them share more than 2 steps.

Eras in sequence: a rater's own driver grows at least 3 eras, each era's pressure taken from the last era's seed of trouble, and each era after the first has at least 2 steps that need technologies of earlier eras.

Earth regrown: with no driver changed (Earth's starting state), the same engine grows, for at least 6 functions, one in each domain, a lineage whose steps match the entries Earth's ledger records for that function, by function and needs and in the ledger's order, in at least 70% of its steps, checked by a repository test whose result is linked from the page.

A sweep: the visitor varies a driver's magnitude (removed, halved, doubled, multiplied tenfold, or a stated continuous range) and the page shows at which value each branch fires or dies, computed from at least 10 runs across the range.

Breadth: lineages are grown for at least 42 drivers, 7 in each of the six domains, with a median of at least 8 steps and no two lineages sharing more than half their steps, and the results file is in the repository and linked from the page.

Reference: one world grows at least 5 eras and at least 60 technologies across at least 4 functions, every step derived by the lab with its rule trace and browsable by era, where a strategy game's technology tree is written by hand and fixed; and at least 5 independent entries in the lab's reference ledger (labs/levels/ledger/alt-reality.json, atlas.json ledger_schema), each opened by the rater at its URL, cite it as a tool for technology worldbuilding.

axes.name: The method's checks
axes.metric: Count of the method's rules computed by code on every lineage the page shows (the Necessity Principle: every need of a step is met by the driver, the world's starting state or an earlier step; why now: every step names a pressure that resolves to a world state; a physics check on every combination; the Orthogonal Path test against Earth's ledger; the driver ablation), whether each violation is shown, refused or repaired, and how the checks score against labelled chains and real outcomes.
axes.how_checked: Read the check code and its tests. Plant each fault through a documented URL flag or a test fixture (a need met by nothing, a step that uses what the driver removed, a pressure that names nothing in the world, a combination whose physics quantity breaks its bound, an Earth ledger entry entered as a step under a new name) and read what the page says. Open the labelled set and the result files named in rungs 7 to 9. Rungs are cumulative.
ladder: No rule is checked on any lineage.
At least one structural rule runs on every lineage shown (one root, one driver, no cycle, every parent a node), and a world that breaks it is refused with the rule's sentence.

At least 6 structural rules run on every lineage (among them: every Earth step pairs with the world step doing the same job, and the artifact is reached from the driver by parent links), each with a repository test that plants its fault and sees the world refused.

The Necessity Principle runs in code: each step lists its needs, every need resolves to the driver, the world's starting state or an earlier step on the same branch, and a step with an unmet need is flagged on the page with the need named.

Why now, cost and physics: every step names its pressure (a scarcity, a bottleneck or a demand) and its cost, a pressure that resolves to no state the driver or an earlier step created is flagged, and every combination carries a physics check computed in code (a named quantity with its unit, from a stated law, compared with a stated bound), with a combination whose quantity breaks its bound shown as killed, with the value and the bound.

Level 5, the fiction made real: every lineage the page shows, the visitor's own included, passes these checks with the result shown per step (needs met, pressure resolved, combination checked), and the Orthogonal Path test marks as Earth-mimicry any step whose function and needs match an entry of Earth's ledger, compared by ids whatever the step is called, so an Earth device under a new name is marked; a step that uses what the driver removed is refused; a documented URL flag plants each fault so a rater can watch it fire.

The ablation runs on the page: reverting the driver to Earth's value marks which steps stop working (an unmet need) or stop being worth building (no pressure), and steps 3 to 5 of every shown lineage are among them.

Each branch carries an orthogonality measure computed against Earth's ledger (the share of its steps with no Earth technology of the same function and needs, or another stated distance), shown with its formula; and on at least 50 labelled chains in the repository (labelled, by readers who did not write the rules, as needing the driver, Earth-mimicry or reasons grafted on), the checks agree with the labels on at least 80%, with the agreement and the misses on the page.

The lab's chains beat both foils: on at least 24 drivers, chains grown by the code the page runs (a test of the method's text in a model's hands alone does not count) beat chains that copy Earth's history and chains whose reasons were grafted on afterwards, on whether their later steps need the driver, by a test whose design, drivers and readers were committed before it ran once; the page states the result in words.

The rules are calibrated on real societies: the rules the page's checks run (the same functions), written blind to the outcomes, run once on a coded sample of at least 500 real societies, name each society's recorded choice among their top two picks more often than the 95th percentile of 10,000 permutations of the environment rows and with a lift of at least 0.10 over the permutation mean, by a gate committed before the run; the page states the result with its source and licence.

Reference: every step on every lineage carries its justification set (the needs, pressure and physics check it stands on), editing or retracting any step re-runs the checks live and marks every downstream step it invalidates, and the checks agree with labels on at least 90% of a held-out set committed only as a hash before the rules it tests were written, and opened after.

axes.name: Artifact from its lineage
axes.metric: How an artifact's form follows from its lineage: the share of its form parameters (shape, material, size, parts; seed, camera and render settings excepted) that a stated mapping derives from lineage steps, needs or the driver, against parameters set by hand; whether its parameter file is validated against its family's schema before anything is built; whether changing one step changes the form; and the quantities computed from the form.
axes.how_checked: Read the artifact grammar, the family schema and the mapping from lineage to parameters. Change one step of a shipped lineage (or the driver's magnitude), regenerate, and diff the parameter file and the drawing. Count traced and hand-set form parameters. Rungs are cumulative.
ladder: No artifact is attached to any lineage.
Each shown lineage ends in a named artifact with its function and a written description of its form.
Each artifact is built by a script from a parameter file and a seed; the same file and seed rebuild the same object, and every build writes a record carrying the parameter file's hash.

Each parameter file is validated against its family's schema (every parameter typed and bounded) before anything is built; a file outside the bounds is refused with the parameter named, and a test holds every committed file to the bounds.
At least 5 form parameters of each artifact are traced in the data to the step, need or driver that sets them, and the trace is listed on the page beside the artifact.

Level 5, the fiction made real: the form is computed from the lineage. A stated mapping derives at least half of an artifact's form parameters from its lineage, each from a property the step provides or needs (a material, a process, a scale, a constraint) and never from a hash or seed of the step's text, so a visitor's own branch yields its own parameter file, validated and drawn at its tip by the same grammar; changing one step of a shipped lineage changes at least 3 form parameters and the drawing.

Each artifact states at least 3 quantities computed from its parameters, with units and the law used (for example light output from glowing area and a published luminance, fuel or water consumed, mass), each tagged REAL or ILLUSTRATIVE, and an artifact whose quantity breaks a stated bound (it could not stand, or could not do its job) is refused.

Families: at least 3 artifact families exist, a schema each; one world's artifacts for different functions share a design grammar derived from its driver (shared materials, joins and motifs named in the data), and a rater shown the uncaptioned drawings of 2 worlds' artifacts sorts at least 9 of 10 into the right world.

Earth's counterpart is built by the same pipeline from a sourced parameter file (its dimensions from a cited museum record or technical drawing of the real device), so the two stand at one measured scale, printed on the page.
An exploded or annotated view labels every part with the step it came from, and removing a step removes or changes the part it set, in a test.

Reference: for at least 20 drivers the artifacts at their tips are generated from their lineages alone (no form parameter set by hand), each passes its schema and its quantity bounds, and the parameter files, records and drawings download as one archive.

G0.evidence: Not a grade of the Orthogonal slice. origin/main at ee4366f holds no labs/orthogonal.html (git show ee4366f:labs/orthogonal.html fails), so nothing this axis measures runs on main. axes.name: Earth's technology ledger
axes.metric: Where Earth's branch and the drivers' facts come from: the count of Earth technologies in one sourced ledger (each with its function, its date, its needs and a source its writer opened), the share of Earth steps on the page read from that ledger rather than typed per world, the count of REAL claims with an opened source against declared gaps, and what is downloadable with its licence.
axes.how_checked: Open the ledger file. Pick 10 entries at random and open each cited source to confirm the date and the dependency. Check that every Earth step on the page resolves to a ledger entry. Count the declared gaps on the page. Rungs are cumulative.
ladder: Earth's branch is absent, or its steps carry no date and no source.
Earth's branch for the shown function is drawn beside the world's, its steps typed in the world's file.
Every Earth step carries a date (a year or a range) and either a source its writer opened or a gap declared on the page.

Earth's steps are read from one ledger file shared by every world: each entry has an id, a technology, its function, a date, its needs (as ledger ids) and a source, and no world file types an Earth step.

The ledger holds at least 60 entries covering every function a shipped world names, each with a source opened (author, year, venue or URL, and the date it was read), and no Earth step on the page carries a declared gap.

Level 5, the fiction made real: for any function a visitor's world serves, Earth's branch for the same job is found in the ledger by function and drawn beside it with Earth's real technologies and dates; the ledger holds at least 150 entries across all six domains; a test checks that every needs link resolves and that no technology is dated before what it needs.

Every real driver a shipped world uses carries its evidence for and against, each source opened and the claim it supports quoted or paraphrased with its page, and the ledger and the driver evidence download as JSON or CSV with their licence stated.
Dates carry their uncertainty and their source's kind (primary, scholarly secondary, encyclopedia), and at least 80% of entries cite a book or a journal article rather than an encyclopedia.

The ledger is audited: where an open dataset of technology dates or prerequisites covers its period, at least 100 shared entries and at least 90% of all shared entries match it within each entry's stated date uncertainty, and the mismatches are listed; where none does, a reader who did not write it checks 50 random entries against their sources and finds at most 5 in error; either way the result is on the page.
At least 500 entries across all six domains from the earliest tools to 1900, and every needs link cites a source that states the dependency, not only the date.

Reference: the ledger is released as a citable open dataset of technology prerequisites (versioned, with a DOI or a stable URL and a licence), and at least 5 independent entries in the lab's reference ledger, each opened by the rater at its URL, use or cite it.

G0.evidence: Not a grade of the Orthogonal slice. origin/main at ee4366f holds no labs/orthogonal.html (git show ee4366f:labs/orthogonal.html fails), so nothing this axis measures runs on main. axes.name: The lineage plate
axes.metric: What the lineage graph draws and links: nodes and edges from data, Earth's branch beside the world's on matched rows, gold only on the branch that fired, the ignition (the branch drawing itself in order and the artifact revealed at its tip), the views a selection lights together, and overlapping labels at 1440 x 900 and 390 x 844.
axes.how_checked: Shoot the page at 1440 x 900 and 390 x 844 at rest, with a step chosen and under reduced motion (node tools/labs-wt.mjs shoot, or tools/drive.mjs). Count overlapping labels on the shots. Choose steps by mouse, touch and keyboard and record what lights. Read the layout code. Rungs are cumulative.
ladder: No lineage is drawn.
The lineage is shown as a list or a static picture.
The lineage is drawn as a node-link graph from data (each edge from a stored parent link), with the branch that fired in gold and Earth's branch dotted in its own lane.

Each Earth step sits on the row of the world step that does the same job; choosing a step by mouse, touch or keyboard shows its reading (its role, note, needs and evidence); no two labels overlap at 1440 or at 390 px.

The ignition: the fired branch draws itself from the driver down in step order and the artifact surfaces at its tip when the line reaches it; under reduced motion or a still flag the finished frame appears at once.

Level 5, the fiction made real: the central scene stands in one plate inside 1440 x 900 without scrolling (the driver at the root, the branching graph with this world's branch in gold and Earth's dotted beside it, the artifact at the tip with Earth's ghosted beside it on one ground line, and the evidence line), drawn with its ignition for any lineage the lab grows, the visitor's own included, up to 25 nodes with no overlapping label, and read in a stated order at 390 px.

Linked views: choosing a step lights its ancestors and descendants, the artifact part it set and its Earth pair; a combination shows both threads meeting; branches that did not fire (killed by physics, or with an unmet need) are drawn ghosted, with the reason on hover and on focus.

Eras on the plate: each era is a band, the seed of trouble is drawn as the hook into the next, an era control redraws the graph era by era, and a world of 60 nodes in 4 eras keeps every label clear at 1440 px and collapses into an expandable outline at 390 px.
A layered layout with crossing minimization (Sugiyama-style) lays out any grown world, and two worlds serving the same function stand side by side, linked step to step by function.

A scenario plays: the world's eras run as a sequence (branches growing, artifacts revealed, each trouble planting the next era) with pause, step and scrub, and the sequence exports as a video or an image sequence.

Reference: the plate exports as SVG and as PNG at print resolution with every mark bound to data, a reader rebuilds the full lineage (every node, edge, need and date) from the exported SVG alone, and at least 5 independent entries in the lab's reference ledger, each opened by the rater at its URL, reuse its plates.

G0.evidence: Not a grade of the Orthogonal slice. origin/main at ee4366f holds no labs/orthogonal.html (git show ee4366f:labs/orthogonal.html fails), so nothing this axis measures runs on main. The slice on branch labs/orthogonal (0b0d3f0, ab68065) gets its first grade from an independent rater after this ladder has had its second pass.

axes.name: Artifact render
axes.metric: How the artifacts look, judged against references each artifact states: the share of branch tips with a rendered still, the references each still is judged against (photographs or drawings of the organism, material or mechanism it is drawn from, and of Earth's device for the same job), whether the light and scale are honest to their tags, and what a tip the visitor grew is given.
axes.how_checked: Open each still at full resolution beside the references its record lists and check each listed feature at plate size. Read each render record (seed, parameter hash, engine, samples, time). Block the image request and look at the fallback. Grow a branch of your own and look at its tip. For rungs 7 and up, run the blind comparisons as written and read their recorded answers. Rungs are cumulative.
ladder: No artifact is drawn.
The artifact is shown as a placeholder, an icon or a stock image.
The artifact at each shipped tip is drawn from its own geometry (an ink drawing or a render) with its title and function, and Earth's artifact for the same job is drawn beside it.

Each shipped tip has a still rendered offline from its parameter file and seed, at most 60 KB at its plate width, with alt text that describes the form; when the image fails to load the same artifact is drawn in ink from its parameter file in the same box, and the page says the picture did not load.

Each still's record names at least 2 references (photographs or drawings of the real organism, material or mechanism it is drawn from, each with its source) and the features taken from them (for a shelf fungus: side-attached caps that overlap, real gills with short gills between, glow on the gill edges and margins), and a rater finds each listed feature visible at plate size.

Level 5, the fiction made real: every tip of every shipped world is a still at prime quality. A rater who did not build it, judging at full resolution against its references and the labs-design skill, finds every listed feature legible at plate size, no look on the skill's list of tells, and light within its tag (a brightness tagged REAL comes from a cited measurement; any brighter light is tagged ILLUSTRATIVE); Earth's artifact stands ghosted beside it on one ground line at a stated scale; Luis's yes on the stills is recorded with its date in the lab's plan or log; and a tip the visitor grew is drawn within 1 s by the same grammar in the plate's ink line and then rendered from its own parameter file with the stills' materials and light (lit and shaded, at runtime or by a render that returns to the visitor's world), with every feature its family's record lists legible at plate size, because the binding says each branch ends in a rendered artifact.
Each still has a detail view (a crop or a second camera on the part its lineage names, such as a gill edge) and a turntable or a set of 3 views, all from the same seed and record.

A blind check: each still is shown, unlabelled and shuffled, beside photographs of real objects of its kind, and at least 3 raters who did not build it judge its material and construction plausible as a made object in at least 80% of their judgements, with the answers recorded in the repository.

A tip the visitor grew cannot be told from the offline stills: in blind pairs at plate size, at least 3 raters who did not build it pick the offline still in no more than 60% of pairs, with their answers recorded in the repository.

Scenes: each shipped world has at least 1 scene of its artifacts in use (a street at night, a workshop), rendered from the same parameter files, with the world's other artifacts placed by the same grammar.

Reference: at least 30 stills across at least 6 worlds, each with its lineage and render record, are published under a stated licence, and at least 5 independent entries in the lab's reference ledger, each opened by the rater at its URL, use or cite them as references for invented technology.

axes.name: Plate language, ink in fog
axes.metric: The craft of the plate in the Contact world's material (ink in fog): the count of style gates above 0 (tools/anti_tells.mjs and the style gates of labs/levels/atlas.json), gold's share of the screen's pixels at rest measured on the screenshots, the number of label grammars on the page, ornament that marks nothing, and the number of the labs-design skill's five design axes on which the plate differs from the other worlds.
axes.how_checked: Run node tools/anti_tells.mjs on the page and count each atlas style gate. Count gold pixels on the 1440 x 900 and 390 x 844 shots at rest. List every label style on the page. Judge the shots with the labs-design skill. Rungs are cumulative.
ladder: No page exists, or the page carries no style of its own.
The page reads the site's tokens file (labs/assets/css/tokens.css) and loads its fonts only from the site's approved hosts.
node tools/anti_tells.mjs reports 0 for the page, and gold falls only on the branch that fired and the chosen step.

One label grammar runs through the nodes, the captions and the reading (one order of name and role, one case, one size ladder), and gold covers under 3% of the screen's pixels at rest at 1440 x 900 and at 390 x 844, counted on the screenshots.
Every atlas style gate counts 0 on the page, and no ornament marks nothing: each corner, rule, frame or bracket marks a state or a measure, as listed in the stylesheet's header or the lab's notes.

Level 5, the fiction made real: the plate is drawn in the Contact material, ink in fog, bound to state (the lineage as ink that draws itself, the artifact surfacing from fog, gold only on what fired), and differs from every other lab world on at least 4 of the 5 design axes of the labs-design skill (geometry, texture, ornament, motion, ink tint), judged at both widths by a rater who did not build it, who names the 4.

Motion follows one stated rule per element (for example the fog clears outward from where the gold strand meets the artifact; ink draws and settles and never blinks in or out), each rule written in the code beside the motion, and reduced motion gives the finished frame.

Each world's plate carries a variation of the material bound to its driver (an ink tint, a line texture or a fog density set by a stated world quantity), so any 2 shipped worlds differ visibly on at least 2 design axes, with each binding listed.
Every state of the product is shot at both widths and holds rungs 2 to 5: an empty world, a world of 60 nodes, a failed render, an era change and two worlds compared.

A designer or illustrator who did not build the lab reviews the plate in a review recorded in the repository, finds no look from the labs-design skill's list of tells, and every finding is fixed or answered.

Reference: the plate language is a documented system (tokens, label grammar, line weights, fog rules) that a second lab uses without editing it, and at least 5 independent entries in the lab's reference ledger, each opened by the rater at its URL, reference the plate, at least one of them a design publication or gallery that features it.

G0.evidence: Not a grade of the Orthogonal slice. origin/main at ee4366f holds no labs/orthogonal.html (git show ee4366f:labs/orthogonal.html fails), so nothing this axis measures runs on main. The slice on branch labs/orthogonal (0b0d3f0, ab68065) gets its first grade from an independent rater after this ladder has had its second pass.

axes.name: World making
axes.metric: The protagonist's verbs from the bindings (change a driver, follow a branch, compare with Earth, grow an era, keep, share), each performed by mouse, touch and keyboard; the kinds of driver the visitor can state; and whether a kept world reopens identically from Labs OS and from a link in a fresh profile.
axes.how_checked: Perform each verb at 1440 px by mouse and by keyboard and at 390 px with touch emulation. State 5 drivers of your own. Keep a world, reload, and open its link in a fresh browser profile; compare the two. Refuse storage and repeat. Rungs are cumulative.
ladder: The visitor can do nothing but scroll.
The visitor chooses a step of a shipped lineage and reads it, by press or by the arrow keys.
The visitor switches between at least 3 shipped worlds, and the world and the chosen step are in the URL, so a link opens the same world on the same step.

The visitor composes a driver from typed fields (domain, the resource or condition, removed or multiplied, magnitude) and sees the composed record before growing it; a driver the lab cannot read is refused with the reason.
A driver stated in one sentence is parsed into that typed record (by rules or by a model), shown and editable before growing; a sentence that cannot be parsed gets the reason.

Level 5, the fiction made real: every verb of the protagonist works from the visitor's own input by mouse, touch and keyboard. The visitor changes a driver, follows a branch step by step, compares it with Earth's for the same job, grows one more era from the last trouble, keeps the world in Labs OS (it reopens after a reload with its driver, branches, eras and artifacts) and shares it as a link that opens identically in a fresh profile; with storage refused, the page says the world lasts until it is closed and the link still shares it.

Editing the output: the visitor edits a step (its need, its pressure or its technology), the lineage regrows from that step, the checks re-run and the artifact's parameters update; undo restores the world before the edit.

Forks: from any step the visitor forks a second world with another driver; the shelf draws the tree of worlds, each child naming its parent and its fork, and any two worlds compare side by side by function.

Of 10 questions of shapes absent from the code's examples (for example "what would this world use for refrigeration", "which step fails if copper is scarce too"), the lab answers at least 7 from its engine and its ledger, each answer with a trace the rater follows to the steps, needs and ledger entries it used, and none contradicting the world's own lineage or its checks.

A world exports as a file (its driver, lineages, eras, parameter files and evidence) and imports identically in another browser, and a second visitor continues a world from its link as a fork of their own.

Reference: a writer builds a world of at least 5 eras and 4 functions in the lab and exports it as a world document (lineages, artifacts, account and evidence), and at least 5 independent entries in the lab's reference ledger, each opened by the rater at its URL, show writers using it.

G0.evidence: Not a grade of the Orthogonal slice. origin/main at ee4366f holds no labs/orthogonal.html (git show ee4366f:labs/orthogonal.html fails), so nothing this axis measures runs on main. The slice on branch labs/orthogonal (0b0d3f0, ab68065) gets its first grade from an independent rater after this ladder has had its second pass.

axes.name: The lab writing on its own
axes.metric: What the lab writes on its own for a visitor's driver (each step's why-now and cost, and an account of how the world came to be), by rule from the engine's trace or by a model route; whether every generated text passes the method's checks before it is shown; what each sentence names as its writer; rejection, repair and fallback rates; and the measured gain of the lab's chains over stated baselines.
axes.how_checked: Read the writer and, if a model is called, the call site of labs/assets/js/ai/llm.js. Grow a driver of your own with a model route and again with the network off, and compare the texts and their writer marks. Plant a reply or a rule output with an unmet need, a removed resource used and an Earth-mimicry step, and check each is refused with its reason. Read the benchmark files and their sealed parts. Rungs are cumulative.
ladder: No part of any world is written by the lab on its own.
Each shown world carries an account of how it came to be, written by hand and tagged as authored.
The account is generated from the lineage: each sentence is tied to a node id, and a test shows that changing a node's data changes its sentence.

For a visitor's own driver the lab writes each step's why-now and cost sentence on its own (by rule from the engine's trace, or by a model route through labs/assets/js/ai/llm.js), and each sentence names what wrote it (the rule id, or the model and the route).

Whatever writes is checked before it is shown: every generated chain and account passes the lab's checks, a failing model reply gets at most one repair call and then falls back to the engine, and the world records per step which of the three happened.

Level 5, the fiction made real: for a visitor's own driver the lab tells how the world came to be, on its own, in an account of at least 150 words written from the chain, every sentence tied to a node and every number to an engine value, naming the pressure behind each step, the two threads of each combination and the trouble the success planted; the account regrows when a step changes, and with the network off it is still written.

axes.name: Engine and render pipeline
axes.metric: Code shape: worlds as data, an engine with no DOM, a render pipeline that is seeded and validated, and what can be added (a world, a driver, a technology, a rule, an artifact family) without touching the engine or the view, counted by adding one of each in a scratch worktree and listing the files each needed.

ladder: No code of this page (orthogonal.html) exists; the earlier page's code (altverse.html) does not count.

Data (worlds), computation (an engine with no DOM) and drawing (a view) are separate modules, and each of the engine's rules lives in one function that the view and the tests both call.
A new world is added as one data file and one line in a list, with no change to the engine or the view, and a test shows the engine refusing a malformed world.

The render pipeline is a script apart from the page (the page loads only committed images, records and parameter files and never runs the renderer), each record names the file's hash, the renderer's version and the render time, and a test recomputes every hash from the committed file and fails when a parameter file changed without a new render.
